wormald.shelfmark: Cambridge, Sidney Sussex College pontifical (no shelfmark given by Wormald)
wormald.wormald_origin: At Durham by the mid-eleventh century, perhaps because Archbishop Oswald took it to York; Wormald suggests it and ‘Claudius I’ may share an origin in the Fenland abbeys (p. 194 n. 134).
wormald.other_contents: Pontifical; begins with ordinations of lesser grades and omits the consecration of bishops (p. 194).
wormald.overview: A pontifical closely related to and slightly older than 'Claudius I' (the VI Æthelred pontifical in Claudius A.iii). Like it, it lacks a rite for consecrating bishops. Its presence at Durham, perhaps via Oswald, leads Wormald to suggest that the two MSS both came from a Fenland abbey rather than from York.
wormald.key_quote: 'their links may be best explained in terms of a common origin in the Fenland abbeys' (p. 194 n. 134)
wormald.doubts: No laws; not in guide. Included only as comparative evidence for Claudius A.iii. Wormald cites it as ed. Banting, Two Anglo-Saxon Pontificals.
verify_notes: Checked p. 194 and nn. 131, 134; origin wording aligned with n. 134 (‘taken to York’), otherwise no changes.
overview: reworded to remove five-word runs matching Wormald’s text.
